investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler. The scheduler message is consistent across all three checks: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and preventing any VM from being assigned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. Because no node can satisfy both constraints simultaneously, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state and no VM ID is ever assigned. This prevents the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") from reaching the point where it can record orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity or configuration condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' for remote-agent-create after 127s unscheduled.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler constraint message after 143s, confirming all three remote-agent checks hit the same infrastructure boundary.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe never advancing past pod scheduling.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming the runner returned no data before the check timed out.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which must schedule a kata peer-pod VM before any evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract at line 256 requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied if the pod never schedules.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=134201 (approx 134s), which exceeds the 127s unscheduled duration reported in the scheduler message, confirming the check exhausted its wait budget on the scheduling stall.
possibleCauses: [Highest evidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. The scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' with no preemption victims available.

[High evidence] Node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets a specific node label or taint that only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are also the ones with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource. If the affinity rules were broadened or additional nodes were labeled, capacity might be available.

[Medium evidence] Cluster under-provisioning: the 6-node cluster may not have enough kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes to handle concurrent eval probes plus any live workload. The fact that all three sibling checks (run sequentially) all hit the same exhaustion state suggests the resource was not freed between runs.

[Low evidence, no supporting source proof] A recent change to node pool sizing, VM quota, or peer-pod provider configuration could have reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, but no infrastructure change records or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to support this hypothesis.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a scheduler configuration or API error.

If the pod spec for remote-agent pods did not request the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, the 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message would point to a different scheduling constraint and the capacity exhaustion hypothesis would not apply.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded and returned all four required evidence keys, the failure would be transient (e.g., a briefly held VM slot was released) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the node affinity rules were found to match more than 2 nodes, the 4-node exclusion count in the scheduler message would indicate a labeling or taint change rather than a static affinity misconfiguration.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed in the same run window, the failure would be isolated to the create path rather than a shared infrastructure capacity problem.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity rules is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 schedulable nodes with available VM slots), alerting before capacity is fully exhausted.

Add a remote-agent pod scheduling latency eval that fails fast (e.g., within 30s) if a pod remains Pending/Unschedulable, rather than waiting for the full outageLatencyMs budget, to reduce mean time to detection for scheduling failures.
Add a stale-pod detection eval that counts remote-agent pods in non-terminal states older than a configurable threshold, catching leaked VM slot holders before they exhaust cluster capacity.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing with Unschedulable Pod
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-30T12:26–12:31Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot place a new kata.peerpods.io/vm pod because 2 nodes report insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and consequently none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the Remote Agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero viable nodes and no preemption candidates available, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod during this eval window timed out as Unschedulable (~127–150 s per attempt), preventing agent creation and making it impossible for the eval runner to collect any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for a new probe pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules restrict scheduling to a subset of nodes that no longer exists or has been relabeled, shrinking the eligible pool to only the 2 already-saturated kata nodes. This would compound the capacity problem.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning for the remote-agent workload class: the 6-node cluster may not have enough kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes to handle concurrent eval probes plus production workloads simultaneously.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — transient spike in remote-agent workload consuming all VM slots at the time of the eval run, with capacity returning afterward. This would be disproved by a passing re-run shortly after the failure window.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler. The scheduler message is consistent across all three checks: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and preventing any VM from being assigned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. Because no node can satisfy both constraints simultaneously, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state and no VM ID is ever assigned. This prevents the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") from reaching the point where it can record orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity or configuration condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' for remote-agent-create after 127s unscheduled.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler constraint message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector') after 144s, confirming the condition persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler constraint message after 143s, confirming all three remote-agent checks hit the same infrastructure boundary.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe never advancing past pod scheduling.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming the runner returned no data before the check timed out.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which must schedule a kata peer-pod VM before any evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract at line 256 requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied if the pod never schedules.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=134201 (approx 134s), which exceeds the 127s unscheduled duration reported in the scheduler message, confirming the check exhausted its wait budget on the scheduling stall.
possibleCauses: [Highest evidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. The scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' with no preemption victims available.

[High evidence] Node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets a specific node label or taint that only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are also the ones with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource. If the affinity rules were broadened or additional nodes were labeled, capacity might be available.

[Medium evidence] Cluster under-provisioning: the 6-node cluster may not have enough kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes to handle concurrent eval probes plus any live workload. The fact that all three sibling checks (run sequentially) all hit the same exhaustion state suggests the resource was not freed between runs.

[Low evidence, no supporting source proof] A recent change to node pool sizing, VM quota, or peer-pod provider configuration could have reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, but no infrastructure change records or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to support this hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the shared infrastructure failure persists across all three checks simultaneously, ruling out an eval-runner-specific or timing-specific issue.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a scheduler configuration or API error.

If the pod spec for remote-agent pods did not request the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, the 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message would point to a different scheduling constraint and the capacity exhaustion hypothesis would not apply.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded and returned all four required evidence keys, the failure would be transient (e.g., a briefly held VM slot was released) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the node affinity rules were found to match more than 2 nodes, the 4-node exclusion count in the scheduler message would indicate a labeling or taint change rather than a static affinity misconfiguration.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed in the same run window, the failure would be isolated to the create path rather than a shared infrastructure capacity problem.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity rules is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 schedulable nodes with available VM slots), alerting before capacity is fully exhausted.

Add a remote-agent pod scheduling latency eval that fails fast (e.g., within 30s) if a pod remains Pending/Unschedulable, rather than waiting for the full outageLatencyMs budget, to reduce mean time to detection for scheduling failures.
Add a stale-pod detection eval that counts remote-agent pods in non-terminal states older than a configurable threshold, catching leaked VM slot holders before they exhaust cluster capacity.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-30T12:26–12:31Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot place a new kata.peerpods.io/vm pod because 2 nodes report insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and consequently none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were written, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the Remote Agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero viable nodes and no preemption candidates available, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod during this eval window timed out as Unschedulable (~127–150 s per attempt), preventing agent creation and making it impossible for the eval runner to collect any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for a new probe pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules restrict scheduling to a subset of nodes that no longer exists or has been relabeled, shrinking the eligible pool to only the 2 already-saturated kata nodes. This would compound the capacity problem.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning for the remote-agent workload class: the 6-node cluster may not have enough kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes to handle concurrent eval probes plus production workloads simultaneously.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — transient spike in remote-agent workload consuming all VM slots at the time of the eval run, with capacity returning afterward. This would be disproved by a passing re-run shortly after the failure window.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on 2 eligible nodes and node affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the stage where it could collect evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out as Unschedulable, preventing the eval from producing any evidence and causing all three remote-agents checks to fail. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect or eval configuration error.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the pod-creation call that triggers scheduling; failure here prevents all downstream evidence collection
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or other consumers have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Supported by all three sibling checks reporting the same 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message across sequential eval runs (12:26, 12:29, 12:31).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, which may indicate a cluster topology change (node labels removed, node pool scaled down, or taint added) that reduced the eligible node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes, amplifying the capacity pressure.

Tertiary — insufficient node pool size for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource class: the cluster may have been provisioned with only 2 nodes carrying this resource, and the per-node VM quota is too low to absorb concurrent eval and production workloads simultaneously.

Lower probability — eval runner scheduling multiple remote-agent pods in rapid succession without waiting for prior cleanup, temporarily exhausting capacity that would otherwise be available. The sequential timing of the three sibling failures (each ~2 minutes apart) makes this less likely as the primary cause but does not rule it out entirely.

recommendedNextActions: Investigate current kata.peerpods.io/vm resource utilization on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes immediately to determine whether capacity is still exhausted or has since recovered.

Identify and terminate any leaked, stuck, or long-running pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that are not actively serving production traffic, to free capacity for new remote-agent pod scheduling.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration on the remote-agent pod spec and the label state of all 6 cluster nodes to determine whether the 4-node exclusion is intentional or the result of a topology change that should be reverted.

Evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota per eligible node or the number of eligible nodes needs to be increased to support concurrent eval and production remote-agent workloads without exhaustion.

Confirm whether the eval runner's withCleanup mechanism (seen at run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) is reliably releasing kata.peerpods.io/vm resources after each probe run, to prevent capacity leakage across successive eval executions.

Because remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true in features.json (lines 183-184) and are also failing, treat this as a required-check failure for the remote-agents feature and escalate accordingly per the feature's outageAfterFailures=2 threshold.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or cluster metrics show that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available and not exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the resource exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved.
If the remote-agent pod spec does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm and the scheduler message is produced by a different mechanism, the diagnosis would need revision.

If re-running the eval immediately after the failure produces a passing result with full evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message present), the failure was transient and not a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector are shown to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the affinity rules are intentionally correct, then the root cause is purely the 2-node capacity limit rather than any affinity misconfiguration.

If a passing run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime is found in history (lastPassingAt is currently null due to no previous run history), it would indicate this is a first-run failure and not a regression from a previously healthy state.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, and reports a distinct 'capacity-unavailable' status rather than timing out.

Add a node-eligibility eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting early if the eligible node pool shrinks unexpectedly.

Add a resource-leak detection eval that checks for remote-agent pods in Pending or Terminating state older than a configurable threshold, to catch cleanup failures before they exhaust capacity for subsequent runs.

Introduce a historical baseline for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime so that currentlyRegressedFromPass can be computed on future runs (currently lastPassingAt=null due to no prior run history).
